title: Rethinking Memory For AI Inference
gist: Edge and physical-AI inference is pushing compute toward memory via PIM (LPDDR6-PIM), PNM (custom HBM4/HBM4E base dies) and CIM, cutting data-movement energy and latency; but broad adoption is years away (~2030) and gated by missing software/compiler/OS support and protocols, added manufacturing cost, and thermal limits that memory makers are addressing with new cooling designs.

insights.claim: The shift of AI from data-center training to edge and physical-AI inference, where sensor data is live-streamed, requires processing data as close to memory as possible to stay within limited power budgets.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Edge/physical AI creates a new design driver for near-memory compute silicon.

themes.theme: PIM vs PNM vs CIM: hardware options and economics

insights.claim: The article distinguishes CIM/IMC (math inside bit cells/bitlines, often analog on SRAM or ReRAM), PIM (digital logic on the same DRAM die, e.g., LPDDR6-PIM, a JEDEC standard nearing completion) and PNM (logic on a separate die in the memory package, e.g., compute on custom HBM4/HBM4E base dies on the roadmap).
